findings.headline: Asset Development Programme has forced professional services costs to revenue, reducing available capital receipts.
findings.detail: The ADP project incurred capital costs that could not be capitalized and were charged to revenue instead. This directly reduces capital receipts available for future schemes. The risk register identifies this as Critical impact with Significant likelihood.
findings.matters: A lender must understand actual capital funding capacity. Revenue-charging of capital costs reduces the council's ability to self-fund future capital investment without borrowing.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - General Expenses Capital Monitoring 2025/26
findings.headline: Lake Terrace Waste Depot environmental compliance works have uncertain budget with cost recovery being pursued
findings.detail: The council has appointed consultants to deliver works mandated by the Environmental Agency, but has explicitly flagged that 'Required amount of budget may change'. Notably, the council is actively pursuing cost recovery, which suggests expectation that costs will exceed the £66k budget. The works are mandatory so will proceed regardless of budget sufficiency.
findings.matters: Mandatory environmental compliance creates committed spending, and the explicit statement that budget may change and costs are being recovered indicates the council's budget estimate lacks confidence. Unbudgeted environmental costs are a tail risk.

findings.quote: Required amount of budget may change. The works will be necessary to meet environmental agency requirement. Recovery of any costs being pursued.

findings.headline: Street Lights Upgrade scheme not progressed and removed from capital programme entirely
findings.detail: A £100k scheme has delivered nothing and is being recommended for deletion rather than carried forward, with the funding reallocated elsewhere. This represents a complete project failure within one financial year, suggesting either poor initial planning or external factors preventing execution.
findings.matters: Project cancellations indicate either weak capital planning or an inability to execute schemes as planned. For a lender assessing capital delivery risk, this is a signal about the council's project management capability.

findings.quote: This scheme has not progressed and is being recommended to be removed from the programme so the funding can be used elsewhere.

findings.headline: Stockyard LUF scheme reprofiled: £11,440k of £11,951k revised budget carried forward to 2026/27
findings.detail: This single scheme represents 80% of the council's total general expenses capital programme. By mid-year only £180k had been spent against the revised budget of £11,951k, with the forecast year-end spend of just £511k. The decision to reprofile indicates the original delivery timeline is not being met. This is the dominant item in the capital programme and its slip affects the entire capital and borrowing profile.
findings.matters: A lender needs to understand actual capital delivery capability and borrowing requirements. A scheme this large running this far behind raises questions about project management, design maturity, and whether the council's financial assumptions are realistic.
findings.figures: Revised Budget 25-26: 11,951 (£'000); Actual April to September 25: 180 (£'000); Year End Forecast: 511 (£'000); Projected Carry Forward: 11,440 (£'000)
findings.quote: This is to be reprofiled.

findings.paper_title: External Audit Findings Report 2024-25
findings.headline: Structural works invoice of £46k completed in 2024/25 not accrued, extrapolating to £77.5k potential error.
findings.detail: Auditor identified that an invoice dated 25 March 2025 for £46k (£38k net) for structural works completed in 2024/25 was not accrued in the financial statements. Due to testing scope, extrapolation suggests a maximum potential error of £77.5k, which exceeds the trivial reporting threshold. The Authority did not adjust despite the amount exceeding trivial threshold.
findings.matters: Accrual principle is fundamental to accurate financial position. A council not accruing for work completed suggests expenditure may be understated and commitments not fully captured.
findings.figures: £46k invoice not accrued; £77.5k extrapolated maximum error
findings.quote: The Authority did not accrue for an invoice received after year end dated 25.3.25 for structural works completed in 2024/25 totalling £46k (£38k net of VAT)... the potential maximum error would be extrapolated to £77.5k which is above our trivial level for reporting.

findings.paper_title: External Audit Findings Report 2024-25
findings.headline: Payables balance overstated by £431k due to incorrect classification of prepayments.
findings.detail: Auditor testing identified that the payables balance included £431k of debit balances relating to prepayments, which should be shown in receivables under CIPFA Code. This was corrected as an adjusted misstatement. Auditor noted extrapolation suggests a further potential maximum error of £192k elsewhere in payables, though not material enough to adjust.
findings.matters: Classification errors affect the shape of the balance sheet and can mask real payment obligations. The auditor's note of further potential errors suggests the classification control needs strengthening.
findings.figures: £431k adjusted; £192k potential maximum additional error identified
findings.quote: The payables balance, which is a credit balance recorded on the balance sheet, included debit balances relating to prepayments... resulted in the payables balance was understated by £431k with a corresponding understatement of the receivables balance of £431k.

findings.paper_title: External Audit Findings Report 2024-25
findings.headline: Old debts of £227k over 5 years old, with only £218k provided for, creating collection risk.
findings.detail: Auditor identified £227k of receivables over 5 years old with only £218k provision made. The age of debt directly impacts collectability and receipt of this income. This issue was also raised in the prior year, indicating it has not been resolved.
findings.matters: A lender assessing cash flow sustainability needs to know how much historic debt is uncollectable. Stale debt represents income that is unlikely to materialise and affects usable reserves.
findings.figures: £227k total old debts over 5 years; £218k provided; £9k unprovisioned
findings.quote: Currently debt over 5 years old totals £227k of which the Authority has provided for £218k. The age of this debt will impact its collectability and subsequent receipt of this income.

findings.paper_title: External Audit Findings Report 2024-25
findings.headline: Finance leases (refuse vehicles from 2018) were not disclosed in prior years, now recognised as £954k asset and £1,081k liability.
findings.detail: IFRS 16 implementation revealed leases for refuse vehicles taken out in 2018 for ten years were previously undisclosed finance leases. These now require a prior period adjustment adding £954k to property plant and equipment and £1,081k to lease liabilities, with £127k adjustment to unusable reserves. This indicates controls over lease identification have been weak.
findings.matters: This represents material liabilities and assets omitted from prior-year statements. It demonstrates the council did not have complete lease records, raising questions about what else might be unaccounted for in capital commitments.
findings.figures: £954k PPE increase, £1,081k lease liability increase, £127k reserves adjustment; 10-year lease from 2018
findings.quote: These leases for refuse vehicles taken out in 2018 for a ten year period... meet the criteria to be included on the Authority's balance sheet as a right of use asset with a related lease liability in 2024/25. As these leases relate back to 2018 this also requires a prior period adjustment as the amount is material.

findings.paper_title: External Audit Findings Report 2024-25
findings.headline: Council dwellings estate (Burnaby Place, Ashfordby) is not registered at land registry, creating legal ownership risk.
findings.detail: Testing of council dwellings rights and obligations identified that the entire Burnaby Place estate has not been registered with land registry. The auditor completed alternative procedures to confirm ownership rights, but notes that not registering assets appropriately creates risk around legal ownership and difficulties with future sales of these dwellings.
findings.matters: A lender or finance director needs assurance that council assets are properly secured legally. Unregistered property creates future encumbrance issues and could affect borrowing security or asset sales.
findings.figures: Burnaby Place, Ashfordby estate; part of £121.4m council dwellings portfolio
findings.quote: Not registering the Authority's assets appropriately could create a risk around legal ownership and in particular difficulties associated with future sales of these dwellings.

findings.paper_title: External Audit Findings Report 2024-25
findings.headline: Property valuations contained material errors totalling £2.8m across formula, area calculations, and rate application.
findings.detail: Auditor testing of land and building valuations identified four material/significant errors: formula errors excluding external works caused £902k understatement; incorrect Gross Internal Areas (GIA) caused £1,911k understatement; wrong BCIS rate applied caused £127k overstatement; investment property formula error caused £234k understatement. Additionally, timing of BCIS rates could mean £72k further understatement.
findings.matters: Melton's property portfolio (£48.5m land/buildings + £121.4m council dwellings + £2.3m investment property) is 62% of total assets. Multiple calculation errors indicate control weaknesses in the valuation process with a new external valuer.
findings.figures: £902k, £1,911k, £127k, £234k, £72k errors; total property portfolio £172.2m (land/buildings £48.48m, council dwellings £121.424m, investment property £2.347m)
findings.quote: Our testing of a sample of land and building valuations identified 3 assets where supporting calculations incorrectly excluded external works due to a formula error... valuations were understated by £902k... a number of discrepancies between the Gross Internal Area (GIA) used by the valuer... resulted in valuations being understated by £1,911k.

findings.paper_title: External Audit Findings Report 2024-25
findings.headline: Auditor issued disclaimer opinion due to no assurance over opening balances from prior year backstop.
findings.detail: The auditor cannot form an opinion on the financial statements because they have no assurance over opening balances for 2024/25. This follows a prior-year disclaimer opinion under backstop legislation. The auditor is unable to conclude whether other information published with the statements (Annual Governance Statement, narrative report) is consistent with the financial statements.
findings.matters: A disclaimer opinion means the auditor cannot verify the starting position for this year's accounts. Any lender relying on audited financials should understand the full audit trail is not assured.
findings.figures: 2024/25 opening balances - no assurance provided
findings.quote: The limitations imposed by not having assurance on opening balances mean that we will be unable to form an opinion on the financial statements. Our anticipated financial statements audit report opinion will be a disclaimer opinion.

findings.paper_title: Minutes , 30/09/2025 Audit and Standards Committee
findings.headline: Deterioration in elected member relationships in 2024/25 is causing distraction and reducing senior officer capacity.
findings.detail: The Annual Governance Statement was amended to note that relationships between some elected members have deteriorated in 2024/25, resulting in distraction and reduced focus for senior officers. This has affected officer capacity and remains an identified action for 2025/26.
findings.matters: Member conflict that affects senior officer capacity undermines the council's ability to focus on delivery and financial management. Distraction at leadership level increases the risk of missed oversight, weaker financial control, and reduced delivery on planned actions.
findings.figures: Member relationship deterioration in 2024/25; capacity impact remains unresolved into 2025/26
findings.quote: a deterioration in relationships between some elected members in 2024/25 and resulting in distraction and focus for senior officers which has affected capacity

findings.paper_title: Minutes , 30/09/2025 Audit and Standards Committee
findings.headline: A governance failure in car parking charge implementation led to three weeks of free parking and exposed weaknesses in oversight and documented procedures.
findings.detail: In March 2025, new car parking charges were misimplemented. Cabinet failed to provide oversight or follow-up at their March meeting. No documented process existed despite the council having undertaken similar changes before. Changes in officer responsibilities led to incomplete handover. To resolve the error, the council operated free parking for three weeks, forgoing revenue. Machines are at end-of-life and scheduled for replacement this year.
findings.matters: This reveals systemic control gaps: the failure occurred despite prior experience, suggesting governance processes do not reliably prevent repeated errors. While new procedures are being put in place, the incident shows a control environment vulnerability that could affect other areas.
findings.figures: Three weeks of free car parking; parking machines at end of life, replacement scheduled this year
findings.quote: There was a failing in oversight from officers and the Cabinet, as they failed to include any confirmation or follow up item in their meeting of 12 March 2025

findings.paper_title: Minutes , 30/09/2025 Audit and Standards Committee
findings.headline: A failing has been identified in the collection of Section 106 developer contributions, now flagged for audit review.

findings.paper_title: Minutes , 30/09/2025 Audit and Standards Committee
findings.headline: Food waste collection implementation is at risk of missing a statutory deadline, with funding uncertainty for vehicles and ongoing revenue costs.
findings.detail: Since the March 2025 report, there has been little progress on food waste collection implementation. The council risks missing a statutory deadline and officers are unsure about penalties. While a capital grant has been received and a project officer appointed, uncertainty remains about new burdens funding for ongoing revenue costs. Officers also note that vehicles are constrained anyway—the wider sector has faced difficulties securing both vehicles and funding for contract changes.
findings.matters: Failure to meet statutory obligations reflects on the council's operational competence and creates delivery risk. Funding uncertainty for an ongoing revenue cost that is not yet resolved creates budgetary exposure.
findings.figures: Capital grant received; project officer appointed; statutory deadline at risk
findings.quote: there has been little progress since the report presented in March and that this report suggested the Council are not going to meet the statutory deadline

findings.paper_title: Appendix B - Car Parking review - follow up questions from Audit and Stanndards Committee
findings.headline: Statutory notice compliance error went undetected until publication and required immediate correction
findings.detail: The first notice of variation was published on 22 May 2025 containing an error (omission of Burton Street Annexe car park). The error was not caught through any internal review process and was only detected on the day of publication. A corrective notice had to be published separately on 29 May. This indicates a failure of quality assurance processes for statutory documents.
findings.matters: Statutory publication errors create legal exposure and demonstrate inadequate review controls for compliance-critical documents; raises broader questions about document quality assurance
findings.figures: Notice published 22 May 2025; error detected same day; corrective notice published 29 May 2025 (one week delay)
findings.quote: The first notice was produced on 20th May and published in the newspaper on Thursday 22nd May. The error was detected on the day of publication (22nd May), and the additional notice to correct the omission was prepared immediately, with the earliest opportunity for it to be published in a newspaper the following week on 29th May.

findings.paper_title: Appendix B - Car Parking review - follow up questions from Audit and Stanndards Committee
findings.headline: Governance failures during November 2024 management restructuring led to loss of ownership of statutory compliance task
findings.detail: A change in reporting lines and director in November 2024, followed by a second director change, removed all senior officers involved in the original planning from active oversight. The new director's handover did not adequately communicate the statutory notice of variation requirement and associated legal advice. This resulted in the responsibility for publishing the notice not being formally reallocated, causing it to be overlooked until too late.
findings.matters: Demonstrates material weakness in how the council manages critical compliance tasks through organizational change; raises questions about whether other statutory or legal obligations may be similarly at risk
findings.figures: Change made 29 November 2024; Cabinet meeting 13 November 2024 delegation to Interim Director; second director change in December 2024; error discovered 22 May 2025
findings.quote: A change to the roles and responsibilities, which had been unforeseen at the time of the legal advice and planning and was made with immediate effect for reasons unrelated to this activity, presented an unusual set of circumstances and a change to the established system. This was then shortly followed by a change in Director, removing all senior officers within the service from the process who had been involved at the time of the planning, with a handover to a new Director which encompassed a wide portfolio. Those officers who had previously been allocated tasks by lead officers continued to deliver upon these in a timely manner, but the failure surrounded a lack of formalised re-allocation of responsibility for the notice of variation element along with the handover of associated legal advice and timetable relating to this.

findings.paper_title: Appendix B - Car Parking review - follow up questions from Audit and Stanndards Committee
findings.headline: Car parking revenue is tracking £50k below budget despite being £90k higher than prior year
findings.detail: The 2025/26 car parking income budget is £140k higher than 2024/25, and year-end income is projected to be £90k higher than the previous year. However, the council is currently tracking a £50k shortfall against the 2025/26 budget projection. Officers attribute some of this to the charge suspension earlier in the year, though acknowledge uncertainty about the exact impact.
findings.matters: Either the budget was materially optimistic or underlying demand is softer than expected; either way, a significant variance between budget and outturn requires explanation
findings.figures: 2025/26 budget £140k higher than 2024/25; projected year-end income c. £90k higher than previous year; currently tracking £50k shortfall in outturn projection
findings.quote: The car parking income budget for 2025/26 is £140k higher than 2024/25, and year end income is projected to be c. £90k higher, and therefore the council is currently tracking a £50k shortfall in outturn projection.

findings.paper_title: Appendix B - Car Parking review - follow up questions from Audit and Stanndards Committee
findings.headline: Unlawful car parking charges resulted in £40k estimated income loss and £3.5k in direct costs
findings.detail: The council published a notice of variation for parking charges containing an error (Burton Street Annexe was omitted). The error was detected on the day of publication (22 May) and residents were charged unlawfully. The council suspended charges during the 21-day statutory notice period and processed refunds. The estimated loss of income from the suspension period was approximately £40k.
findings.matters: Revenue income was materially disrupted by operational and compliance failures, and the incident raises questions about internal controls and process oversight
findings.figures: Direct costs £3.5k; estimated income loss c. £40k; error detected 22 May 2025, corrective notice published 29 May 2025
findings.quote: The direct costs of the error was £3.5k covering the cost of the investigation and additional advertising costs. The estimate provided at the time was that the loss of income was c. £40k for the period where charging was suspended (inc refunds).

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Internal Audit Progress Report
findings.headline: Risk management framework compliance rated Moderate (Amber) despite sound overall design, with gaps in application including weak project risk management and missing target dates for mitigation actions
findings.detail: The audit of risk management found the council has a generally sound control environment but significant gaps in how the framework is applied. Governance documents need updating, project risk management is weak, and critical control gaps exist: risk owner responsibilities are not formally defined in policy documentation, and mitigation actions lack consistently recorded target completion dates, limiting tracking of progress.
findings.matters: A Moderate/Amber compliance rating means the risk management framework is not consistently operating as intended. Poor tracking of mitigation completion dates and weak project risk management reduce the council's ability to identify and respond to emerging financial risks, which concerns lenders assessing the council's resilience to adverse events.
findings.figures: Compliance assurance: Moderate (Amber); Control environment: Good (Green); Organisational impact: Low (Green)
findings.quote: there is scope for improvement in relation to application of the framework. These areas include the need to update governance documents, improve accessibility and version control, and strengthen project risk management... mitigation actions are monitored, but target completion dates are not consistently recorded, limiting the ability to track progress effectively

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Internal Audit Progress Report
findings.headline: 21 audit recommendations remain overdue for implementation, including one high-priority action overdue for more than three months
findings.detail: Of 30 agreed audit actions, only 9 have been completed since the last committee meeting. 21 actions are now overdue, with 16 (53% of the total) more than three months late. The breakdown shows particular weakness with medium-priority actions: 12 of 19 (63%) are overdue by more than three months. One high-priority recommendation has exceeded its implementation deadline by over three months, indicating a critical control weakness is not being remedied.
findings.matters: Audit recommendations not being implemented signals management is not addressing identified control gaps. A high-priority action stalled for 3+ months suggests the council is ignoring material control risks to its operations and financial management—a governance failure that directly affects creditworthiness.
findings.figures: 21 overdue actions out of 30 total; 16 actions (53%) overdue for more than three months; 1 high-priority action overdue for more than three months; 12 of 19 medium-priority recommendations (63%) overdue more than three months

findings.paper_title: External Audit Value for Money Report 2024/25
findings.headline: Procurement compliance with the new Procurement Act 2023 is incomplete, with audit finding only moderate controls
findings.detail: Internal Audit identified that the Council needs to improve compliance with the Procurement Act 2023, which came into force in February 2025. Three recommendations were raised, including reviewing guidance and policies, updating the contracts register (with two spending items not matched to contracts), and providing procurement training. The Council intends to implement all three by end of November 2025.
findings.matters: Procurement control weaknesses can lead to overspending, poor contract management, and regulatory risk. Non-compliance with statutory procurement law could trigger enforcement action.
findings.figures: Three procurement recommendations; implementation deadline 30 November 2025; nine exemptions during 2024/25, highest value £0.09m
findings.quote: Internal Audit note there is scope to review guidance and policies to ensure compliance with the Procurement Act 2023 which came into effect in February 2025. Internal Audit also note two discrepancies where spending could not be matched to the contracts register and recommend a wider review of arrangements to ensure the register is kept up to date.

findings.paper_title: External Audit Value for Money Report 2024/25
findings.headline: Financial forecasting accuracy is weak, with £1.08m movement between February forecast and March outturn
findings.detail: In the final quarter of 2024/25, the Council's General Fund forecast changed by £1.08m on a net expenditure base of £6.42m. While this resulted in a surplus rather than deficit (showing prudence), it demonstrates significant forecasting volatility. Officers have taken steps to improve forecasting discipline, but the scale of the movement raises questions about budget holders' engagement and planning discipline.
findings.matters: Lenders rely on councils' quarterly finance reports to monitor position. Large variances between forecast and outturn undermine confidence in the reliability of management's financial information and in-year control.
findings.figures: £1.08m movement on £6.42m forecast net expenditure; this equates to 16.8% variance in the final quarter
findings.quote: The General Fund saw a total movement between mid February and the end of March of £1.08m on forecast net expenditure of £6.42m, which is significant.

findings.paper_title: External Audit Value for Money Report 2024/25
findings.headline: The council is re-tendering its housing repairs contract after significant contractor underperformance
findings.detail: The Council's housing repairs and maintenance contractor delivered poor service, leading to tenant complaints and a decision to terminate and re-procure. In Q1 2025/26, the HRA is forecasting a £0.14m overspend, including a £0.2m repairs and maintenance overspend, with £0.13m relating to unpaid invoices from 2024/25 that the contractor only submitted after the year-end.
findings.matters: Lenders should know about housing service delivery problems, as they affect both resident satisfaction and the council's HRA finances. Contract failures indicate procurement or contract management weaknesses.
findings.figures: Q1 2025/26 HRA overspend forecast £0.14m; repairs and maintenance overspend £0.2m; delayed invoices from prior year £0.13m
findings.quote: The forecast includes a £0.2m overspend on repairs and maintenance, with £0.13m relating to 2024/25 invoices submitted by the contractor. The Council has taken appropriate steps to address this, including agreeing with the contractor to terminate the agreement and re-tender the service.

findings.paper_title: External Audit Value for Money Report 2024/25
findings.headline: The Council has a £4m cumulative funding gap forecast across the medium term with no credible plan to bridge it
findings.detail: The Medium-Term Financial Strategy forecasts in-year deficits of £1.11m (2026/27), £1.32m (2027/28), and £1.54m (2028/29), totalling around £4m. The Council's Corporate Priorities Reserve, which stood at £2.66m on 31 March 2025, would be exhausted by the end of 2027/28. The Financial Sustainability Plan currently delivers only £0.16m in savings (1.5% of budgeted expenditure), insufficient to address the gap.
findings.matters: Lenders need to know whether a council has a credible plan to return to financial sustainability. Without additional income or service reductions, the council will run out of reserves and lack a buffer against unexpected pressures.
findings.figures: £4m cumulative deficit forecast; Corporate Priorities Reserve £2.66m; 2026/27 deficit £1.11m; 2027/28 deficit £1.32m; 2028/29 deficit £1.54m; current savings plan £0.16m (1.5% of £10.5m budgeted expenditure)
findings.quote: The Council recognises the need to develop additional income generation or savings schemes to bridge the £4m cumulative funding gap forecast in its Medium-Term Financial Strategy. Current plans do not support this, and difficult decisions are needed to ensure that the Council does not continue to use reserves to balance the budget.

findings.matters: Overdue audit actions suggest the council is not addressing control weaknesses or governance issues identified by internal audit. A lender assessing credit risk would want to know whether management is promptly implementing audit recommendations, as this reflects the control environment and financial governance.
findings.figures: 21 agreed management actions overdue; 76% overdue for more than three months

findings.detail: The council forecasts homelessness overspend of £84k, comprising £52k on bed-and-breakfast accommodation and £39k on rent deposit schemes. This is only partially mitigated by £13k Asylum Dispersal Grant, indicating sustained housing pressures and rising demand.
findings.matters: Growing cost in statutory provision; council absorbing costs rather than reducing service; indicates sustained housing pressures and increasing demand for emergency accommodation.

findings.paper_title: General Fund Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring Report 2025/26, Quarter 2
findings.headline: Anticipated £500k capital receipt from cattle market land sale not received; council switching to external borrowing
findings.detail: The LUF Stockyard project was financed partly through expected capital receipts from the cattle market land sale (circa £500k), which has not yet been received. Rather than wait, the council has decided to fund the shortfall through external borrowing, representing a material shift from receipts to debt financing.
findings.matters: Unplanned increase in council debt; indicates tighter short-term cash position; changes financing profile and may affect medium-term borrowing capacity.
findings.figures: £500k anticipated capital receipt not received, £1m total capital receipts budgeted for Stockyard project
findings.quote: The sale of the cattle market land has not yet been received. The remainder of this anticipated capital receipt (circa £500k) was to be used for a variety of other capital projects and allocated accordingly in the programme. As the budgeting process has now commenced for 2026/27 it is therefore prudent to change the funding to external borrowing.

findings.detail: Biffa's proposed food waste collection model requires five vehicles costing £658k total. DEFRA funding covers only four vehicles at £409k. The council acknowledges this as a service requirement but must fund the £250k shortfall, creating a capital scheme in trouble with no identified funding solution.
findings.matters: Capital scheme overspend with mismatch between service requirement and available resources; will likely require additional borrowing to bridge the gap.
findings.figures: £250k overspend, £658k total cost, £409k DEFRA funding available
findings.quote: Biffa's latest proposed food waste collection model would require five vehicles at a total cost of £658k. The available funding from DEFRA is £409k based on four vehicles, leaving a potential overspend of £250k.

findings.figures: £27k fire insurance overspend

findings.detail: Agency staffing costs are dispersed across multiple teams: £85k in Repairs & Maintenance for vacant post coverage, maternity leave, and long-term sickness; £11k in General Management for interim Senior Income Officer cover; £11k in Special Services for vacant posts and long-term sickness. The small amount of vacant post savings are fully utilised for agency staff to cover those posts whilst vacant, in addition there is also agency cover for a long-term sick post and an additional officer to cover maternity leave, at this time the estimated over spend is in the region of £85k.

findings.paper_title: Housing Revenue Account Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring Report 2025/26, Quarter 2

findings.detail: The council identifies as High Risk that it cannot fully cleanse repairs commitments from the Northgate housing system, and that further unaccrued contractor charges from 2024-25 may arise. The absence of a financial interface between the contractor and repairs team is hampering efforts to account for all outstanding commitments.

findings.paper_title: Housing Revenue Account Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring Report 2025/26, Quarter 2

findings.detail: The council budgeted for 150 voids but has completed 100 by September with 100 more expected (200 total). Average void cost increased from £3.5k to £4k. A value for money review found the current voids contract does not represent value for money, triggering re-procurement. The overspend reflects 50 more voids than budgeted plus cost per void inflation.
findings.matters: Voids represent a loss of rent income and high reinstatement costs; re-procurement mid-cycle signals contract failure and budget setting risk

findings.paper_title: Housing Revenue Account Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring Report 2025/26, Quarter 2

findings.detail: Biffa's food waste collection model requires five vehicles costing £658k total, but DEFRA grant funding provides only £409k for four vehicles. This leaves a £250k gap being formalized through a decision notice that is currently being drafted.

findings.headline: Waste management contract inflation budgeted at 3% but actual 0.3%, with October-March inflation unknown until February 2026

findings.paper_title: Appendix A for Housing Revenue Account Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring Report 2025/26 Quarter 1
findings.headline: Repairs & Maintenance is forecast to overspend by £201,000 in 2025/26
findings.detail: Although Q1 spending on Repairs & Maintenance was £593,465 against a quarterly allocation of £775,226, the year-end forecast predicts full-year spend will reach £3,441,320 against a budget of £3,240,320. This £201,000 overspend is the principal driver of the HRA's expenditure variance and represents 6.2% of the maintenance budget.
findings.matters: A maintenance cost overspend of this magnitude indicates either deteriorating housing stock condition, inflation in repair labour and materials, or increased responsive repair demand. This directly affects debt servicing capacity and future asset investment headroom.
findings.figures: £3,240,320 budgeted; £3,441,320 year-end forecast; £201,000 overspend

findings.figures: £66k current budget allocation

findings.detail: The £9.965m original allocation (£11.951m revised) has achieved only 0.6% spend in first quarter. Project is currently under review with update promised later in year. Minimal progress raises delivery risk on significant capital commitment.

findings.figures: £9,965k original budget, £62k actual spend Q1, £11,951k revised budget

findings.paper_title: Appendix B for General Fund Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring Report 2025/26, Quarter 1
findings.headline: Food waste vehicles project is forecasting £250k overspend with no identified funding source
findings.detail: Council budgeted £409k for vehicles but needs 5 vehicles at estimated cost of £658k. Government funding covers only 4 vehicles at lower cost. Year-end forecast shows £831k spend against £581k budget (vehicles plus caddies). The £250k shortfall is unresolved.
findings.matters: Unmatched capital overspend requires immediate funding decision; affects capital headroom and may trigger reserve drawdown or slippage to future year

findings.paper_title: Housing Revenue Account Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring Report 2025/26 Quarter 1
findings.headline: Independent Living Charge implementation delayed and reduced, creating £9k income shortfall.
findings.detail: The Independent Living Charge was not applied until week 3 of the financial year (21 April 2025) and has been applied at a lower amount than approved. If this continues through the year, it will result in a £9k shortfall.
findings.matters: Income policy implementation is lagging and below approved levels, compounding revenue pressures.
findings.figures: £9k expected shortfall
findings.quote: The independent Living Charge was not applied until 21 April 2025 (week 3) and was applied at a lower amount than approved, if this continues for the year then a shortfall of £9k is expected.

findings.paper_title: Housing Revenue Account Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring Report 2025/26 Quarter 1
findings.headline: Capital programme underspend of £1.69m, driven by planning permission delays and scope reductions.
findings.detail: £670k to carry forward. Two major projects (Douglas Jane Meeting Room and Fairmead Community Centre) are delayed awaiting planning permission. Energy Efficiency grant funding came in £1.02m below budget, reducing the total project cost from £1.52m to £500k and requiring a 3-year delivery schedule.
findings.matters: Capital deferrals delay service improvements and suggest either planning/permitting issues or scoping uncertainty. Smaller grant receipt reduces headroom for future maintenance.
findings.figures: £1.69m total underspend; £670k carry forward; Energy Efficiency reduced from £1.52m to £500k
findings.quote: The funding granted for this project was less than hoped so the total project cost will be £500k, of which £250k is grant funded. The project may span over a 3 year period with contracts put in place by the end of this financial year.

findings.paper_title: Housing Revenue Account Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring Report 2025/26 Quarter 1
findings.headline: Affordable housing purchase plan scaled back, creating £30k rental income shortfall.
findings.detail: Cabinet approved purchase of 5 new affordable rental properties (June 2025 meeting), but this was a reduction from the originally planned 8 properties that were cancelled. Even with the 5-property purchase, a £30k annual rental income shortfall is expected.
findings.matters: Income targets are being missed due to asset acquisition delays or scope reduction. The mitigation is only partial.
findings.figures: £30k shortfall; 5 properties approved (down from 8 planned)
findings.quote: The now cancelled capital purchase of 8 affordable rented properties is causing the shortfall on the affordable housing rental income. Cabinet approved the purchase of 5 new properties at its meeting on 10 June 2025 which are expected to partly mitigate this but a shortfall of around £30k is still expected.

findings.paper_title: Housing Revenue Account Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring Report 2025/26 Quarter 1
findings.headline: Fire insurance costs jumped £27k annually due to high number and value of fires in housing properties.
findings.detail: Fire insurance has increased by £27k compared to budget, attributed explicitly to 'the high number and value of fires in our housing properties over recent years'. This is a component of the £63k General Management overspend.
findings.matters: Repeated fires signal either property quality issues, maintenance backlogs, or tenant behaviour problems — all indicate underlying portfolio risk.
findings.figures: £27k increase in fire insurance
findings.quote: The fire insurance figures have been confirmed as £27k over that budgeted, the increase in costs is due to the high number and value of fires in our housing properties over recent years.

findings.paper_title: Housing Revenue Account Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring Report 2025/26 Quarter 1
findings.headline: Contractor financial control weakness: 'absence of an interface' preventing accurate accounting of repairs commitments.
findings.detail: The council's repairs contractor has no integrated financial system with the housing management system (Northgate), hampering the ability to track all outstanding commitments. Risk is rated High/Critical for further unaccrued charges from 2024-25, and a tender exercise for a new contractor will address this but the current position remains unresolved.
findings.matters: A broken financial interface with the repairs contractor creates audit and forecast risk. The council cannot confirm it has accrued all liabilities.
findings.figures: High/Critical risk rating; already £130k of unaccrued 2024-25 charges discovered
findings.quote: The absence of an interface for financial aspects between the contractor and the repairs team is hampering efforts to ensure that all outstanding commitments are adequately and fully accounted for.

findings.paper_title: Housing Revenue Account Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring Report 2025/26 Quarter 1
findings.headline: Repairs and Maintenance overspending by £201k, including £130k of unresolved 2024-25 void costs.
findings.detail: The £201k overspend includes £130k relating to 2024-25 void works (clearances, electrics, asbestos removals) still being settled, plus £38k agency cover for staffing gaps and maternity leave, and £33k additional software maintenance costs following vendor renegotiation.
findings.matters: Void costs rolling over from prior year signal either weak forecasting or problematic properties. Software costs jumped 33% suggesting budget assumptions are stale.
findings.figures: £201k total overspend; £130k 2024-25 voids; £38k agency staffing; £33k software
findings.quote: While the 2024-25 voids accruals continue to be worked through and paid, a further £130k relating to clearances, electrics and asbestos removals for 2024-25 has been submitted by the contractor. An overspend on computer equipment software maintenance of £33k is now anticipated, this is due to the increased annual charge following renegotiation of our main software supplier and an increase in licensing requirements.

findings.paper_title: Housing Revenue Account Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring Report 2025/26 Quarter 1
findings.headline: HRA revenue overspend of £144k forecast, reducing contributions to reserves.
findings.detail: Budget holders project a £188k net cost overspend, partially offset by additional investment income of £44k, leaving a net £144k overspend. This is managed by reducing the planned contribution to the Regeneration & Development Reserve while maintaining the approved working balance of £1m.
findings.matters: Revenue overspend erodes financial flexibility and forces a choice between reserves or service reduction. The working balance buffer is being drawn upon.
findings.figures: £144k overspend (£188k cost overspend less £44k investment income); approved working balance £1m
findings.quote: As of 30 June 2025, budget holders are projecting a forecast revenue overspend for the HRA of £144k, which includes additional £44k in respect of investment income. Overall this will result in a reduced contribution to the Regeneration & Development Reserve in order to maintain the approved working balance of £1m.
